# std/dns.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from std/dns.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

The IPv4 address of a host name, for programs on the
hosted target: the query and the reader of core/dns.bastio, over a TCP
connection to a resolver on port 53 (DNS over TCP, RFC 7766, which every
recursive resolver answers; it needs no UDP in `host_net`). The resolver
comes from the caller or from /etc/resolv.conf; the message id is random
(`net_random`). Only A records, no search domains, no cache, no DNSSEC; the
answer is as trustworthy as the path to the resolver (HTTPS authenticates
the server whatever address the lookup gave).

`import "std/dns.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/endian.bastio](core-endian.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md), [core/dns.bastio](core-dns.md), [std/net.bastio](std-net.md), [std/host.bastio](std-host.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`dns_lookup_via`](#dns_lookup_via) | The IPv4 address (as `net_ip4` makes it) of the host `name`, asked of the resolver at `resolver` (port 53, over TCP). |
| [`dns_lookup_at`](#dns_lookup_at) | `dns_lookup_via` for a resolver that listens on `port`. |
| [`dns_system_resolver`](#dns_system_resolver) | The first IPv4 nameserver of /etc/resolv.conf, if the file is there and has one. |
| [`dns_lookup`](#dns_lookup) | The IPv4 address of the host `name`. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `dns_lookup_via`

```bastio
fn dns_lookup_via(h: &Host, resolver: u64, name: &Bytes) -> Option[u64]
```

The IPv4 address (as `net_ip4` makes it) of the host `name`, asked of the
resolver at `resolver` (port 53, over TCP): `None` if `name` is not a
valid host name, nothing answers, or the answer holds no A record.

Example:

```bastio
// Nothing listens on port 53 of the loopback in the test setup (or it
// does not know this name): either way no address comes back.
let name = bfrom("no-such-host.invalid");
let mut bad = 0;
match dns_lookup_via(host, net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1), name) {
  Option::Some(ip) => { bad = 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(name);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `dns_lookup_at`

```bastio
fn dns_lookup_at(h: &Host, resolver: u64, port: u64, name: &Bytes) -> Option[u64]
```

`dns_lookup_via` for a resolver that listens on `port`.

Example:

```bastio
let name = bfrom("no-such-host.invalid");
let mut bad = 0;
match dns_lookup_at(host, net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1), 1, name) {
  Option::Some(ip) => { bad = 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(name);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `dns_system_resolver`

```bastio
fn dns_system_resolver(h: &Host) -> Option[u64]
```

The first IPv4 nameserver of /etc/resolv.conf, if the file is there and
has one.

Example:

```bastio
// Either a nameserver is listed or the file has none; both are fine.
match dns_system_resolver(host) {
  Option::Some(ip) => { if ip == 0 { return 1; } },
  Option::None => {},
}
```

### `dns_lookup`

```bastio
fn dns_lookup(h: &Host, name: &Bytes) -> Option[u64]
```

The IPv4 address of the host `name`: a dotted-quad address is returned as
it is, then /etc/hosts is read (`dns_hosts`; `localhost` is always
127.0.0.1), then the system's resolver is asked (see `dns_system_resolver`).

Example:

```bastio
let lo = bfrom("127.0.0.1");
let mut bad = 1;
match dns_lookup(host, lo) {
  Option::Some(ip) => { if ip == 2130706433 { bad = 0; } },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(lo);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

## Internals

### `dns_exchange`

```bastio
fn dns_exchange(h: &Host, sock: u64, id: u64, q: &Bytes) -> u64
  requires blen(q) <= 512 && id < 65536
```

Internal: sends the query `q` (id `id`) over `sock` and reads the length
-prefixed response, up to 64 KiB. The address in the answer, 0 if there
is none or anything fails.
